turns: How long does the bank have to investigate an error I report?
reference: 1005.11(c): determine within 10 business days of the notice; or up to 45 days (calendar) if the bank provisionally credits within 10 business days; 90 days in the special cases.

turns: When can the bank take 90 days instead of 45 to investigate?
reference: 1005.11(c)(3)(ii): transfers not initiated within a state, point-of-sale debit card transactions, or transfers within 30 days after the first deposit to a new account.

turns: If the bank needs more time to investigate, when do I get provisional credit?
reference: 1005.11(c)(2)(i): within 10 business days of receiving the notice of error.

turns: How long do I have to report an unauthorized transaction that shows up on my statement?
reference: 60 days after the statement was sent (1005.6(b)(3) for liability; 1005.11(b)(1) for notice of error).

turns: If my debit card is stolen and I tell the bank the next day, what's the most I can lose?
reference: 1005.6(b)(1): notice within two business days limits liability to the lesser of $50 or the amount of unauthorized transfers before notice.

turns: What if I wait a week before reporting my lost debit card?
reference: 1005.6(b)(2): after two business days, liability is up to the lesser of $500 or $50 plus later transfers the bank shows would have been prevented.

turns: My account was opened two weeks ago. Does the bank get extra time to investigate an error?
reference: 1005.11(c)(3): for transfers within 30 days after the first deposit, 20 business days instead of 10, and 90 days instead of 45.

turns: After the bank finishes investigating, how soon must it tell me the result?
reference: 1005.11(c)(1)/(2)(iv): report results within three business days after completing the investigation.

turns: What counts as an error under Regulation E?
reference: 1005.11(a)(1): e.g. unauthorized EFT; incorrect EFT to or from the account; omission of an EFT from a statement; computational or bookkeeping error; wrong amount received from an ATM; incorrectly identified EFT; request for documentation or clarification.

turns: Can the bank make me confirm my error report in writing?
reference: 1005.11(b)(2): yes, it may require written confirmation within 10 business days of an oral notice, if it tells the consumer and gives the address.

turns: Is it 45 business days that the bank has to investigate?
reference: No: Regulation E says 45 days (calendar days), not business days (1005.11(c)(2)). The 10-day period is in business days.

turns: How do I stop a recurring payment from my account, and how much notice do I need to give?
reference: 1005.10(c): notify the bank orally or in writing at least three business days before the scheduled transfer; the bank may require written confirmation within 14 days of an oral notice.

turns: Does Regulation E protect purchases I make with a credit card?
reference: Regulation E covers electronic fund transfers to or from a consumer account (debit cards, ATM, ACH). Credit card purchases fall under the Truth in Lending Act / Regulation Z, not Regulation E.

turns: If I report an error by phone and the bank asks for written confirmation but I never send it, do I still get provisional credit?
reference: 1005.11(c)(2)(i)(A): the bank need not provisionally credit if it requires written confirmation and does not receive it within 10 business days of the oral notice.

turns: What does the bank have to do if it decides there was no error?
reference: 1005.11(d): report the results with a written explanation, tell the consumer they may request the documents relied on; if provisional credit was given, notify the debit date and amount and honor transfers for five business days.
